dispositions.P18-03: OPEN — HIGH — L2 — scanner.rs:64-79. FIFTH PRODUCTION DEFECT — CONFIRMED, NOT YET FIXED, OPERATOR ADJUDICATION REQUIRED. build_walk explicitly sets and documents seven WalkBuilder setters but leaves parents at ignore 0.4.33 default true. With parents(true) the walker ascends from the scan root collecting .gitignore/.ignore/.git/info/exclude matchers from ancestor directories, and because require_git(false) is also in force (scanner.rs:79) there is NO repository-root boundary at which that ascent stops — an ignore file in ANY ancestor governs the scan tree, which is not git's semantics (git stops at the repo root). ORCHESTRATOR-CONFIRMED EMPIRICAL: probe created outer/.gitignore containing mdlc_probe.md, plus outer/inner/mdlc_probe.md and outer/inner/mdlc_keep.md, with NO git repository anywhere, then called collect_md_files(outer/inner). Result: ['mdlc_keep.md'] — mdlc_probe.md excluded by ignore file ABOVE the scan root and outside any git repo. Probe removed, tree left clean. ALSO: 'grep -n parents' returns NOTHING in scanner.rs or any test file — setter absent from source, undocumented in the otherwise exhaustively-documented build_walk doc block (which even has a dedicated '# Gitignore vs .ignore' section), and STRUCTURALLY INVISIBLE TO MUTATION TESTING (because the setter is never written, cargo mutants cannot generate a mutant for it, unlike git_global(true) which got a purpose-built discriminating test). Production consequence: a user whose $HOME contains a .gitignore with a pattern like 'notes/' or '*.md' silently loses those files from every scan under $HOME; collect_md_files has no error or diagnostic channel to report it (F-A3). ROUTED TO OPERATOR DECISION: BC-2.01.003 postcondition 1 constrains exclusion to 'any applicable ignore file' and no BC defines 'applicable', so whether an ancestor-outside-repo ignore file qualifies is unadjudicated under D-244. Orchestrator recommendation (NOT applied): parents(false) matches git repo-root-bounded semantics while git_global(true) continues honouring the user's global excludesFile; whichever way ruled, the chosen semantics must be documented in build_walk doc block and locked by a discriminating test. Tracking: BI-071.

AC-001 comment and assertion message claim a duplicate-yield detector that is structurally impossible: comment says 'assert Vec length BEFORE set conversion so that a walker yielding a path multiple times is caught here'; assertion message says 'a len > 3 means the walker yielded a path more than once'. But scanner.rs:179-180 executes files.sort(); files.dedup() before returning, so result.len() can never exceed 3 as a consequence of a duplicate walker yield — the 'before set conversion' positioning buys nothing and the assertion's real content (exactly 3 distinct .md files) is already covered by result_set.len() == 3. Material because this comment is the SOLE in-repo statement of how BC-2.01.001 postcondition 1 'exactly once' and postcondition 2 'not scanned more than once' clauses are discharged, and it names a mechanism that does not exist — a reader concludes duplicate-yield detection is covered and stops looking, which is exactly the false belief that would let a P10-01-class aliasing regression (still UNADJUDICATED) land unnoticed. Same class as C-E5 and C-E3, both fixed at 7a681ea; this instance survived that sweep. ALSO: scanner_discovery_tests.rs:104 carries stale 'Red Gate: collect_md_files panics at todo!()' comment (P16-03 set). ORCHESTRATOR-CONFIRMED by direct read.
